findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night rather than cumulatively, with the threshold set at 90% (versus CD's 70% cumulative standard). Damages are billed at 100% of the room rate for every unoccupied room, not a formula-based fraction, and no relief is given for the shortfall relative to the whole block. The hotel's occupancy records are declared final and binding, with Group expressly waiving any audit or verification right, and there is no cross-credit between F&B overage and room attrition.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition should be measured cumulatively across the entire block with liability only below 70% pickup, using a formula-based calculation, sellout-night credit, and Group audit rights.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block of 340 rooms. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed group room rate ($289.00) plus applicable tax, calculated as the lesser of the number of unsold rooms in the Hotel that night or the shortfall between Group's minimum block and actual pickup. For any night the Hotel achieves 95% occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment for that night. At Group's request, Hotel will provide supporting occupancy records to verify the calculation. Any excess food and beverage revenue above Group's F&B minimum will be credited against room attrition damages, and vice versa.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis, with shortfalls calculated by comparing actual rooms occupied to the block size on each night of the event period. Group shall be deemed in attrition if actual occupancy falls below the attrition threshold of ninety percent (90%) on any night.
findings.exposure_basis: If Group achieves 0% pickup vs. contract's night-by-night 100%-rate liability across the full 340-room, 4-night block at $289/night ($289 x 340 x 4 = $392,840), versus CD's cumulative 70%-of-rate structure only below 70% pickup — worst-case exposure difference calculated on full block value at 100% vs. reduced 70%-threshold formula.

findings.finding_text: The contract declares the Hotel's occupancy and registration records final and binding, and expressly bars Group from auditing, verifying, or inspecting those records or contesting the Hotel's attrition calculation on any basis.
findings.cd_standard: Group should have audit rights and a formula-based, not discretionary, damages calculation.
findings.proposed_language: At Group's request, Hotel will provide supporting occupancy records, including registration cards and room-by-room occupancy logs, to verify any attrition calculation, and Group retains the right to contest the Hotel's calculation in good faith.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's occupancy records, registration cards, and room-by-room occupancy logs shall not be open to Group for audit, verification, or inspection, and Group waives any right to independently verify the Hotel's calculations or to contest the Hotel's occupancy records on any basis.

findings.finding_text: Cancellation damages are calculated as a percentage of gross room revenue (not room profit), with no floor for cancellations more than 12 months out (the schedule starts charging 25% at 365+ days), no duty to mitigate/resell, and no rebooking credit — the contract expressly forecloses all of these.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be a sliding scale against room profit (70% of rate), with no liability beyond 12 months out, hotel mitigation duty with credited resale proceeds, and a rebooking credit.
findings.proposed_language: In the event of cancellation, liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit — defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed group room rate of $289.00 — on a sliding scale based on days prior to arrival, with no liability for cancellation more than twelve (12) months prior to arrival. Hotel will undertake reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and food and beverage functions, crediting resale revenues less substantiated transaction costs against the cancellation fee. Should Group rebook the Hotel within one (1) year of cancellation, Hotel will credit 100% of the resulting room revenue toward damages owed. Any award for breach is limited to actual damages; punitive damages will not apply.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall be liable to the Hotel for liquidated damages calculated as a percentage of gross room revenue that would have been earned by the Hotel for all guest rooms for all nights within the event period
findings.exposure_basis: Full room block gross revenue exposure at 100% cancellation tier: 340 rooms x 4 nights x $289.00 = $392,840, versus CD standard calculating against 70% of rate (room profit) with mitigation credits.

findings.finding_text: The contract explicitly states there is no liability-free window at any point after execution, directly conflicting with CD's standard of no liability for cancellation beyond 12 months prior to arrival.
findings.cd_standard: No liability for cancellation more than 12 months prior to arrival.
findings.proposed_language: No liquidated damages will apply for cancellation notice given more than twelve (12) months prior to the arrival date.
findings.quoted_text: no period of time following execution shall be deemed a liability-free window during which cancellation would occur without incurring liquidated damages

findings.finding_text: Force majeure is narrowed to events that render performance 'physically impossible' and expressly excludes government travel restrictions/advisories, epidemics/pandemics, and attendee safety concerns — the opposite of CD's required inclusions. Deposits and payments are also expressly forfeited rather than refunded upon force majeure termination.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure should explicitly include government travel restrictions/advisories, epidemics/pandemics, and unsafe-to-travel circumstances, with deposits refunded promptly.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability if performance is rendered illegal, impossible, or commercially impracticable due to: acts of God; war; government regulation, advisory, or authority; disaster; strikes; civil disorder; curtailment of transportation facilities; epidemic or pandemic; or any other emergency, including circumstances making it unsafe, illegal, or imprudent for attendees to travel to or assemble at the Hotel. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) business days of the notice of termination.
findings.quoted_text: government-issued travel restrictions, travel advisories, or governmental directives limiting group gatherings or travel, regardless of the reason such restrictions or advisories are issued; epidemics, pandemics, or declarations of public health emergency, including any government responses thereto; or concerns among Group members regarding attendee safety, willingness to travel, or health considerations

findings.finding_text: The contract states the deposit and initial payment are retained by the Hotel despite termination due to force majeure, with no refund or credit issued for prior payments.
findings.cd_standard: Deposits should be refunded promptly upon force majeure termination.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) business days of the notice of termination due to force majeure.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel's only obligation upon occurrence of force majeure shall be to release Group from performance obligations prospectively; no refund or credit shall be issued for payments previously made

findings.finding_text: The cutoff date is set at 45 days prior to arrival, exceeding CD's 21-30 day standard, and reservations after cutoff are only available at rack rate rather than group rate subject to availability.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff should be no earlier than 21-30 days prior to arrival, with post-cutoff reservations remaining available at the group rate subject to availability.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to the group's arrival date. After the cutoff date, the Hotel will continue to accept reservations at the group rate on a space-available basis.
findings.quoted_text: Reservations for rooms within the block committed for the National Association of Coastal Engineers event shall be accepted by the Hotel only when received on or before forty-five (45) days prior to the arrival date

findings.finding_text: Relocated guests bear all costs of alternate lodging and transportation at their own expense, receive no upgrade or amenity upon return, and relocated nights are expressly excluded from pickup, occupancy, and commission credit — contrary to CD's standard across every element.
findings.cd_standard: Walked guests should receive hotel-funded comparable accommodations, transportation, message forwarding, a welcome amenity and upgrade on return, with the relocated night credited toward pickup/commission and no attrition liability.
findings.proposed_language: If the Hotel is unable to accommodate a guest with a confirmed reservation, the Hotel will, at its own expense, provide comparable or better accommodations, complimentary round-trip transportation, message forwarding, and upon return an upgrade and welcome amenity. Each displaced room will be credited toward Group's final pickup and remain commissionable, and Group will not be liable for attrition damages for any relocated night.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall make a reasonable effort to secure alternative lodging at the guest's sole expense and cost

findings.finding_text: The Hotel reserves the right to impose new fees at any time, including after signature, and states Group must pay them 'whether or not such fees were disclosed prior to Group's signature' — directly contrary to CD's requirement that undisclosed charges be waived.
findings.cd_standard: All mandatory fees must be disclosed prior to signature; any undisclosed charge should be waived outright.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will disclose in writing, prior to execution of this Agreement, all charges associated with the Event, including resort fees, surcharges, shipping and delivery, telephone access, and setup/rental charges. Any charge not disclosed to Group in writing prior to signature is waived.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall pay all such fees as added to its bills, whether or not such fees were disclosed prior to Group's signature on this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: A $35.00 per-room, per-night resort fee is charged even on complimentary room nights that Group earns, effectively negating the value of the complimentary room benefit.
findings.cd_standard: Mandatory fees must be disclosed and should not be layered onto complimentary rooms in a way that erodes an already-negotiated benefit.
findings.proposed_language: The resort fee will not apply to complimentary room nights awarded to Group under this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: This resort fee is in addition to all room rates and shall be applied to every room night, including complimentary room nights that Group may receive.
findings.exposure_basis: Estimated 4-night block at 1 comp room per 75 paid nights implies at least a few comp rooms; $35/night resort fee applied to comp nights adds direct cost. Approximate calc: (340*4)/75 ≈ 18 comp room nights x $35 x avg multiple nights ≈ estimate not precise, left conservative.

findings.finding_text: Any F&B shortfall is billed at 100% of the difference rather than a fraction, and menu pricing is locked in 24 months before the event rather than the 12-month maximum CD's standard allows.
findings.cd_standard: F&B minimums should lock pricing no earlier than 12 months out, and shortfalls should be billed at 35% of the gap, not the full difference.
findings.proposed_language: Menu prices for the Event's food and beverage functions will not be established earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event. If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, not the full shortfall.
findings.quoted_text: The parties agree that the Hotel shall provide Group with menus and pricing no later than twenty-four (24) months prior to the Event dates.

findings.finding_text: Complimentary rooms are awarded at 1-per-75 (versus CD's 1-per-40), are left to the Hotel's 'sole and absolute discretion,' can be withdrawn without notice, and are entirely forfeited if the block commitment (100% occupancy) is not met.
findings.cd_standard: Complimentary rooms should be earned on a clear, cumulative 1-per-40 formula, not subject to hotel discretion or forfeiture due to attrition.
findings.proposed_language: Group will receive one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) occupied, revenue-producing room nights actualized, calculated cumulatively across the entire room block, regardless of whether the contracted block was otherwise met.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide complimentary room nights to Group based on a ratio of one (1) complimentary room per seventy-five (75) paid room nights occupied during the Event Period.

findings.finding_text: Assignment requires the Hotel's consent, withheld in its 'absolute discretion for any reason whatsoever, or for no reason at all,' with no carve-out for a successor management company or affiliated entity.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to assign the contract to a successor management company or affiliated entity without unreasonably withheld consent.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations under this Agreement and the event dates, room block, and program remain substantially unchanged. Any other assignment requires Hotel's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel's consent to any proposed assignment is entirely within Hotel's sole discretion and may be withheld in Hotel's absolute discretion for any reason whatsoever, or for no reason at all.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel disclaims any duty to disclose planned renovation/construction and expressly bars Group from terminating, claiming damages, or seeking a rate reduction regardless of how disruptive the work is.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should represent no current renovation plans, commit to 30 days' notice with mitigation details, and allow Group to terminate without liability if the work interferes with the event.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel represents it has no plans for renovation affecting Group's space other than ordinary maintenance. If Hotel later confirms such plans, it will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days describing scope, schedule, impact, and mitigation plan. If Group determines the work will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no representation, warranty, or guarantee regarding the status, scope, timing, or impact of any construction, renovation, maintenance, or capital improvement work

findings.finding_text: The contract sets the finance charge at 1.5% per month compounding, versus CD's 1% per month (or legal max, whichever is less) cap, and provides no defined dispute window before finance charges accrue and no defined prepayment percentage if credit isn't approved.
findings.cd_standard: Late finance charges on undisputed balances should be capped at 1% per month or the legal max, whichever is less, with a real dispute window, and a defined prepayment percentage if credit isn't approved.
findings.proposed_language: If payment of undisputed charges is not received within thirty (30) days of the final invoice, a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, will apply. Group will have thirty (30) days to review and dispute charges before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount. If credit is not approved, prepayment will be limited to a defined percentage of estimated charges, with the balance due at departure.
findings.quoted_text: a monthly finance charge of 1.5% shall accrue on the unpaid balance, calculated from the due date until payment is received in full by the Hotel. This finance charge shall compound monthly

findings.finding_text: Pickup reports are given only 'upon Group's written request and at the Hotel's convenience,' with no periodic reporting required, and Group's audit and inspection rights over room block records are expressly waived.
findings.cd_standard: Group should get weekly pickup reports before cutoff, a full post-event report within 30 days, and a no-cost room block audit right.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting a set number of days prior to the cutoff date, and a full post-event report within thirty (30) days of departure. At Group's request, Hotel will conduct a face-to-face room block audit at no cost, comparing the Hotel's in-house guest list against Group's registration list.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall have no right to audit, inspect, or verify the Hotel's room block records, reservation systems, or internal accounting related to Group's event, and Group waives any audit rights it might otherwise possess under applicable law or contract principles.

findings.finding_text: Indemnification runs one-way from Group to Hotel and extends to claims arising from the Hotel's own negligence (not just gross negligence/willful misconduct), while the Hotel expressly declines to indemnify Group under any circumstance.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual and limited to each party's own negligence or willful misconduct; the group should never indemnify the hotel for the hotel's own negligence.
findings.proposed_language: To the extent permitted by law, each party will protect, indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party against claims arising out of the negligence or willful misconduct of the indemnifying party in connection with the Event. Neither party indemnifies the other for that other party's own negligence.
findings.quoted_text: This indemnification obligation shall extend to claims arising from the Hotel's own negligence in its provision of services or maintenance of premises

findings.finding_text: The $25,000 security deposit can be applied against attrition, F&B shortfalls, and cancellation penalties — expressly commingled with unrelated charges — and refund is delayed to 90 days rather than the standard 30-day window.
findings.cd_standard: Security deposits should be refunded within 30 days absent documented damage, and should not offset attrition, cancellation, or F&B shortfalls.
findings.proposed_language: The security deposit will be refunded in full within thirty (30) days of the event's conclusion unless Hotel provides an itemized accounting of specific, documented damage. The deposit may not be applied toward attrition, cancellation, or F&B minimum shortfalls.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel may apply the security deposit, or such portion thereof as necessary, against any attrition charges, food and beverage shortfalls, damages to the Hotel's premises, incidental costs, outstanding room charges, service failures, cancellation penalties, or any other sum that the Group owes to the Hotel
findings.exposure_basis: Full $25,000 security deposit is exposed to being applied against attrition/cancellation/F&B shortfalls rather than held for damages alone.

findings.finding_text: The contract collapses all termination — including termination for the Hotel's uncured material breach — into the cancellation liquidated-damages scale, and additionally holds Group liable for the Hotel's lost profit and consequential damages upon Group's termination for cause.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause should let Group walk away with no liability and a prompt refund, entirely separate from the cancellation clause's liquidated-damages scale.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) business days, upon force majeure, labor dispute, material change in ownership/management/brand, or Hotel's uncured material breach. None of the foregoing triggers the liquidated-damages calculation in the cancellation clause.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the grounds upon which Group effects termination, whether for cause, convenience, or otherwise, any and all termination by Group shall be deemed and treated as a cancellation subject to the cancellation damages scale set forth in this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: The contract gives Group only a 10-day window (versus CD's 30-day standard) to terminate after receiving notice of a brand/ownership/management change, and expressly excludes bankruptcy, foreclosure, or receivership from triggering any notice or termination right at all.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should notify Group within 30 days of a brand/ownership/management change or bankruptcy/foreclosure, and Group should have 30 days to terminate without liability.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel undergo a material change in ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or file for bankruptcy, or have foreclosure occur, Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days. Group may terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice, with all deposits refunded within five (5) business days.
findings.quoted_text: the Group acknowledges that the Hotel may be subject to bankruptcy, foreclosure, receivership, or other insolvency proceedings, and that such events shall not trigger any notice requirement, termination right, or remedy available to the Group

findings.finding_text: The Hotel has no obligation to disclose collective bargaining expiration dates or actual labor disputes, and Group has no cancellation right for a labor dispute of any kind, contrary to CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should give a year's advance notice of CBA expirations and prompt notice of disputes; a strike/lockout/expired contract within 90 days of the event should let Group cancel with no liability.
findings.proposed_language: One year in advance, Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year, and will notify Group within ten (10) working days of becoming aware of any labor dispute. If a strike, lockout, or expired labor contract arises within ninety (90) days of the Event, Group may cancel without liability, with all deposits refunded promptly.
findings.quoted_text: the Group shall have no right to cancel this Agreement based upon the occurrence or threatened occurrence of any such labor-related event

findings.finding_text: The Hotel retains an unrestricted right to sell to the public below Group's rate, and any rate adjustment applies only prospectively (not retroactively) and is expressly excluded from commission, pickup, and attrition credit.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should guarantee no lower public rate during event dates; if breached, Group's rate should be adjusted retroactively without losing commission or pickup credit.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees it will not sell guestrooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted group rate during the Event dates, excepting qualified rates. If Hotel offers a lower rate, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match, and such rooms remain fully commissionable and creditable toward Group's pickup and attrition calculation.
findings.quoted_text: No retroactive adjustment to Group's rate shall apply to reservations already confirmed prior to the date on which the lower rate is identified.

findings.finding_text: The contract uses 'gratuity' and 'service charge' interchangeably with no separate definitions, and the Hotel retains sole discretion on whether any portion is distributed to staff at all.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be clearly and separately defined, with gratuity fully distributed to staff and service charge disclosed as hotel revenue.
findings.proposed_language: Any gratuity charged to Group's account will be fully distributed to staff assigned to the Event. Any service charge is separate from gratuity, is not distributed as a tip, and is retained by Hotel. Both charges and their percentages will be disclosed to Group in writing.
findings.quoted_text: the terms 'gratuity' and 'service charge' shall be used interchangeably throughout this Agreement and are not separately defined

findings.finding_text: The Hotel expressly disclaims any duty to attempt resale of released inventory, and any resale revenue is retained in full by the Hotel with no credit against Group's damages, and no records are made available to Group.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should have an affirmative, documented duty to resell canceled rooms and credit proceeds against damages owed, with records available to Group.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues, less substantiated transaction costs, against any cancellation or attrition damages owed by Group. Records documenting this mitigation effort will be made available to Group upon request.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall have no obligation to attempt to resell such released inventory or function space, nor shall the Hotel be required to undertake any specific actions, marketing efforts, or promotional activities directed toward filling released space

findings.finding_text: Group is required to use only Hotel-appointed vendors and is subject to a $2,500 surcharge per unauthorized outside vendor engagement.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use the outside vendor of its choice at no additional fee or surcharge.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services or rentals including but not limited to audio-visual, exhibit decorating, security, floral, transportation, and tours. Hotel's in-house vendors are not mandatory for any service category.
findings.quoted_text: Group's use of any outside vendor in violation of this requirement shall incur a surcharge of $2,500.00 for each such engagement.
findings.exposure_basis: Stated surcharge per unauthorized vendor engagement in the contract.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel disclaims any ADA compliance warranty and places sole responsibility on Group to assess accessibility and fund auxiliary aids anywhere in the Hotel, with no obligation on the Hotel for its own common areas or guest rooms.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should warrant ADA compliance of guest rooms/common areas/function space, indemnify only for its own ADA obligations, and fund auxiliary aids in guest rooms/common areas while Group funds function space aids.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel warrants that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with the ADA's public accommodation requirements. Group is responsible for auxiliary aids needed in function space; Hotel is responsible for auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no representation, warranty, or covenant regarding the accessibility of its facilities under the Americans with Disabilities Act

findings.finding_text: Governing law and venue are fixed to Maryland (the Hotel's location, not Group's), the Hotel is entitled to punitive damages, and the 'prevailing party' fee-shifting provision is skewed to deem the Hotel prevailing if it recovers any material relief.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law/venue should be the group's location, with no punitive damages and each party bearing its own fees.
findings.proposed_language: This Agreement will be construed under the laws of the state in which Group is located, with disputes settled in a court of law in the city in which Group is located. Any award will be limited to actual damages; punitive damages will not be awarded. Each party will bear its own attorney's fees.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall be entitled to recover, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity and in addition to any actual damages awarded, an award of punitive damages to the extent permitted by applicable law

findings.finding_text: The Hotel is expressly authorized to use attendee data for its own marketing and to share it with affiliates and third-party marketing providers without further Group consent.
findings.cd_standard: Attendee data should not be used by the hotel for its own marketing or sold/shared with third parties without Group's consent.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will use rooming list and attendee data solely to fulfill reservations under this Agreement, and will not use such data for its own marketing purposes nor disclose it to any third party without Group's prior written consent.
findings.quoted_text: Group acknowledges that the Hotel may utilize such attendee data for the Hotel's own marketing, promotional, and business development purposes

findings.finding_text: The named storm clause requires Group to forfeit its deposit entirely upon invoking the cancellation right, even though the cancellation is penalty-free in name — this deposit forfeiture functions as a penalty contrary to the intent of a no-liability named-storm right.
findings.cd_standard: A named storm clause should allow cancellation without liability upon a storm warning within a defined window before the event.
findings.proposed_language: Should Group invoke the named storm cancellation right, Hotel will refund the deposit paid, less any documented non-recoverable costs already incurred, within a reasonable period after cancellation.
findings.quoted_text: Should Group invoke the named storm cancellation right, Group shall forfeit the deposit paid to the Hotel, which shall be retained by the Hotel as partial compensation for the Hotel's lost revenue and costs incurred in preparation for the event.

analysis.document_notes: This is a heavily one-sided draft that systematically inverts CD's standard positions across nearly every clause category — attrition, cancellation, force majeure, walk/relocation, mandatory fees, indemnification, audit rights, ADA, labor, governing law, and vendor exclusivity are all drafted to maximize hotel discretion and minimize hotel obligation, with repeated express waivers of Group's audit, dispute, and termination rights. Several clauses (attrition, cancellation, termination for cause) are also cross-referentially stacked so that a single triggering event (e.g., termination for the Hotel's own breach) is treated as a full cancellation exposure. Given the volume and consistency of one-sided drafting, this document should be treated as a starting point for substantial renegotiation rather than a near-final draft with isolated issues."
